team_submit: Record a node you executed yourself. Claimed changed_files are cross-checked against the worktree; stage_ok comes back adjudicated, never raised. Idempotent per {run_id, node_id, attempt}: a duplicate call for a finished node is a no-op that returns the stored verdict (`idempotent: true`). Pass `attempt` for a stricter check (rejected on mismatch).
team_retry: Open a fresh attempt, carrying the rejection feedback forward. With subgoal_id, retries that subgoal. With node_id naming a failed report node, reruns just that report (optionally away from avoid_executors). With neither, retries the spec (setgoal + critique). When the retry budget is gone the failure is settled: every node that needed its output becomes `unreachable` and the report becomes ready.
tm_open: Open a task for a request that may be too large for one graph run. Spawns a daemon that drives the whole task (size, shape, critique, package dispatch, integrate, goal gate, report) under ~/.harness/tasks/<task_id>/. The caller never drives a node: watch with tm_status/tm_board/tm_events, or block briefly with tm_wait. Prefer tm_run unless you also want tm_next's node-by-node reply.
tm_run: Open a task exactly like tm_open and spawn the same daemon, but never self-drive and never return a node table: just {task_id, run_id, docs_dir}. For a caller that hands off a whole request and walks away; follow up with tm_wait, or tm_status/tm_board any time.
tm_next: Which manager nodes are ready (each with a briefing_path) plus every running child as {cwd, run_id, driver}. Executes a ready dispatch node here (worktree, child run, headless driver) and services dead drivers: just poll again. Never drive a child yourself; tm_submit the dispatch node once its child stops. A daemon-driven task is left to the daemon.
tm_wait: Bounded long-poll on a daemon-driven task: blocks up to max_ms and returns the node transitions (finished nodes, newest last) since `cursor`, or an empty list on timeout - never the full state. Pass the previous reply's `cursor` back to continue (omit or 0 starts from the beginning). Call again while `state` is "running"; stop when it is "complete" or "blocked".
tm_submit: Record a manager node: pass the payload the fresh agent returned; a dispatch node takes none, the manager folds the child run's verdict. Refused while the child runs with a live driver, or is waiting_capacity (tm_retry({reset_capacity:true})). Pass `key` (a TASK key from tm_inbox) instead of node_id to answer a waiting_human card. Idempotent per {task_id, node_id, attempt}.
tm_retry: Open a fresh attempt. package_id: a new dispatch in the same worktree, carrying the rejection forward. repackage: [ids] after an integration conflict. repair: true after integrate came back verified=false with no conflicts. reset_capacity: true respawns drivers parked waiting_capacity after a usage-limit death. With none, continues from the node that stopped the graph or resumes a dead daemon.
tm_file: File one or more develop STORYs against a task that has already reached goal level (a gate:goal node exists): the path a QA-found defect takes (a fresh package per story, its own dispatch/accept chain, a fresh integrate and goal gate behind it), but filed with reporter "user" / origin "tm_file". Never counted against qa_rounds, so it always proceeds.
tm_board: Ticket-shaped board. Omit task_id for every EPIC (key, name, state, phase), grouped by `initiative` as `groups: [{initiative, key: "I-<slug>", epics}]` when any task has one, else a flat `{epics}` list. With task_id: the EPIC header plus its STORY kanban (one row per package) and a doc_path to INDEX.md (may not exist yet; see tm_docs). task_id accepts a run id or the key E-xxxxxxxx. Read-only.
tm_ticket: One ticket by key: I-<slug> for an initiative (every EPIC under it, with state and cost), E-xxxxxxxx for an EPIC (with its `name`), E-xxxxxxxx/Pn for a STORY. Returns state, worktree/branch, task progress (x/y) and the last accept verdict, plus doc_path (EPIC/STORY) and reporter/origin/link (STORY). Read-only.
tm_log: Follow one ticket's log as readable lines, newest last. key E-xxxxxxxx/Pn: the STORY's latest driver stream, one line per event (E-xxxxxxxx/S for a size-S task's single run). key E-xxxxxxxx: the task ledger (as tm_events). Reads only the last `tail` lines (default 50, max 500). Pass the previous reply's `cursor` as `since` for only newer lines; raw:true returns exact lines. Read-only.
tm_assign: Pin a card to a human, or release it back to auto. `key` is a STORY (E-xxxxxxxx/Pn, every subgoal in it) or TASK (E-xxxxxxxx/Pn/subgoalId) key; a TASK key needs its child run to exist. `to: "human"` (optionally `who`) pins the AUTHOR stage only (implement/draft/cases), never a judging stage, and parks it in waiting_human. `to: "auto"` releases it back to pending.
tm_inbox: Two sections. `cards` is every waiting_human card across every task (or one, with task_id): TASK ticket key, title, what is asked (acceptance criteria, briefing_path), assignee and since when. Complete one with tm_submit({task_id, key, payload}). `decided` is every card a MODEL tried to pin that a non-interactive run sent to an AI instead; object with tm_assign. Read-only.
tm_docs: (Re)render the phase markdown under <docs_dir>/E-<task8>/ from task.json (INDEX, request, shape, critique, one page per STORY, integrate, goal gate, report), whichever have data. rebuild:true DELETES THE ENTIRE EPIC DOCS DIRECTORY FIRST, then writes every file fresh; by default files are overwritten and a stale one from a dropped package survives. The md is a view; the engine never reads it back.
tm_clean: EPIC teardown: removes the worktrees and local branches a finished task's packages created. With task_id: refused while the task runs (tm_wait first, or wait: true); dry_run defaults false. Without task_id: sweeps every terminal task; dry_run defaults true. Never touches the integration worktree/branch; a package branch is deleted only once merged into it or HEAD, else listed in kept_branches.
tm_cancel: Stop a running, blocked or partial task for good: marks it cancelled, kills its daemon, drivers and judges (confirming every pid dead), retires its child runs, writes a report stub (80-report.md) and appends daemon_done then `clean`. The task reads `cancelled` (terminal); tm_retry and tm_submit refuse it. Worktrees and branches stay for tm_clean. A no-op on a finished task.
tm_ask: For a running STORY's own driver: ask the TeamLeader a question the briefing and the plan do not settle. It parks the driver - end your turn right after the call; you are resumed at no cost with the answer in your prompt. The TeamLeader answers from the plan and wiki, or forwards to the person. Refused for an empty question, a key that is not a STORY of this task, or a STORY that is not running.
tm_post: Post one message on the task's bus. `from` is your own STORY key (E-xxxxxxxx/Pn), never `teamleader` or `person`. `to` is a STORY key, `teamleader`, `person` or `all`. A STORY may post only to a sibling STORY or the teamleader: never the person (use tm_ask), `all`, itself or a finished STORY. Body 1-8192 chars. Refusals read `tm_post refused: <reason>`. Returns `ts` and topic.
tm_read: Read the task's bus as `key`: a STORY key sees messages to it, from it and to `all`; `teamleader` and `person` see every message (a driver may not read as those). Pass the previous reply's `cursor` (last ts seen; 0 or none starts at the beginning) for only newer ones. At most 50 per call, oldest first; `more: true` means call again with the returned cursor. Refused as `tm_read refused: <reason>`.
tm_hold: Hold or resume a task on purpose. action `hold` (reason required) records task.hold and starts no driver until `resume`; a driver mid-turn finishes. `resume` lifts it and raises the daemon. Refused for a held, done, cleaned or cancelled task (hold) and for an unheld task (resume).
